articles.title_orig: Siri AI Gets More Capable in iOS 27.3
articles.title_zh: Siri AI Gets More Capable in iOS 27.3
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27 just made your iPhone a lot more capable.
The iPhone is easy to recommend to anyone looking for great smartphone hardware and long-term software support. The previous few iOS releases, however, have been pretty janky. With iOS 27, Apple therefore shifted its focus to ironing out bugs and improving overall stability rather than cramming in another round of flashy new features, and a good chunk of the WWDC 2026 keynote covered improvements such as snappier app launch times, faster AirDrop transfers and better memory management.
Apple's commitment to software updates also means iOS 27 compatibility extends all the way back to the iPhone 11, which is great news since iOS 26 would have been a terrible final major update to be stuck on. If you haven't already updated your iPhone, you can do so by navigating to Settings > General > Software Update .
Not much has changed visually, which makes sense since Apple only recently overhauled its design language with Liquid Glass. There is now a system-wide transparency slider, though, which many users had been asking about. Reports about battery life are mixed — some say they're getting less screen-on time than before, while others haven't had issues. Personally, iOS 27 has been such a blessing performance-wise on my aging iPhone 15 Pro Max that I'm willing to put up with slightly worse battery life.
Of course, stability upgrades aren't the only thing Apple introduced with iOS 27. The update also brings a handful of useful tidbits, and here are five features you should definitely check out after updating your iPhone.
Apple Intelligence has had a rocky start. After all, it took Apple two whole iOS generations to deliver on its promises of a more capable Siri. Most of the Apple Intelligence suite has been pretty underwhelming, unless you're one of the five people who enjoy generating custom emojis using Genmoji , but iOS 27 changes that. The Shortcuts app has received a major upgrade, and Apple Intelligence might finally have a genuinely useful feature to show for itself.
You've been able to create pretty complex shortcuts and automations on iOS for a while now, and you can even import shortcuts that others have created and shared. iOS 27 now lets you create shortcuts using natural language prompts, which Apple Intelligence handles. When you launch the app and tap the + button, you can start describing the shortcut you want.
In my testing, the integration works pretty well and usually creates straightforward shortcuts without issues. That said, it pieces together the wrong actions sometimes and ends up with a shortcut that doesn't do exactly what you want. Fortunately, you can still manually tweak shortcuts created using Apple Intelligence by tapping Edit .
You can also use Apple Intelligence actions within your shortcuts. Apple currently offers three AI models, including an on-device model for faster processing. You can create shortcuts for actions involving information extraction, summarization or generation of text and documents. The Cloud and Cloud Pro models do have a daily rate limit, though.
The Wallet app on the iPhone stores your payment cards, transit passes, event and cinema tickets, digital keys and more. Until now, users could only add digital passes and credentials if the issuer supported Apple Wallet and provided a compatible pass. While several companies and services offered this convenience, plenty of issuers didn't support it. As a collector, I was a bit disheartened to see my local IMAX theater stop offering Apple Wallet passes for movie tickets.
With iOS 27, you can create custom passes and add them to Apple Wallet. This is extremely handy for those with loyalty cards or gym memberships that don't offer native Apple Wallet support. There are two ways you can create a pass in Apple Wallet, and Apple Intelligence comes in handy again here. On supported iPhone models, you can open an image (or screenshot) of a ticket or membership card with a barcode, swipe up and tap on Add Pass to Wallet .
If this option doesn't show up, you can also open the Wallet app, tap the + icon at the top and select Create a Pass . Tap on Continue and take a photo of the ticket or ID card. The Wallet app will then use Visual Intelligence to extract relevant information from the image and create a pass. If you want to change the pass' details or visuals, tap Edit.
For years, Apple's virtual assistant, Siri, has lagged behind competitors like Google Assistant. Slow responses are forgivable, but Siri would often struggle with even the most basic requests. Apple first promised a major Siri overhaul with iOS 18's Apple Intelligence suite, but it's taken over two years to come to fruition. iOS 27 comes with Siri AI , and users with a compatible iPhone can join the waitlist by navigating to Settings > Siri . The AI-powered virtual assistant is still in beta, but things are already starting to look promising.
Siri now understands and fulfills your requests noticeably better, with a huge improvement in how it handles follow-up queries. Though it still takes a hot second to process most requests, its responses are more relevant, and it doesn't hit you with the "Here's what I found on the web" reply as often. What's more impressive about Siri AI, though, is the fact that it now understands personal context.
It can pull information from your messages, emails, photos and more to answer questions or perform tasks that previously required you to manually dig through different apps. Third-party app support is still limited, but if you mainly use iMessage and the default Mail app on your iPhone, you'll likely find Siri to be one of iOS 27's biggest improvements. The Camera app has a new Siri mode as well, which taps into Visual Intelligence to answer questions about whatever you're pointing your camera at.
The AirPods are some of the most popular wireless earbuds on the market, and they work best when paired with an iPhone, iPad or Mac. Most modern AirPods models support Spatial Audio with head tracking, and several music streaming services like Apple Music and Tidal let you enjoy Dolby Atmos content. Sound quality is also widely regarded as one of their strongest selling points, particularly on the higher-end Pro models like the AirPods Pro 3 that we reviewed. With iOS 27, though, you can finally tweak the sound to your liking using a built-in equalizer.
Apps like Apple Music have long allowed you to apply EQ presets, but the new AirPods equalizer works system-wide. The feature is available on AirPods 4 and newer, AirPods Pro 2 and newer and the AirPods Max 2. Connect your AirPods to your iPhone, launch the Settings app, tap on the AirPods settings at the top of the screen and navigate to Audio & Routing > Equalizer .
The Recommended option is selected by default, which delivers the balanced sound profile you've grown used to. If you tap on Custom , you can manually adjust the lows, mids and highs to your liking. If you prefer thumpy bass, increase the lows slider, but if you want vocals to sound clearer, try bumping up the mids or highs instead. Though Apple is only offering a 3-band equalizer, it's still a welcome addition. My AirPods Pro 2 already deliver punchy lows, but as a basshead, I appreciate having the option to crank up the bass even further.
Apple's latest mobile OS also has several additions that make browsing more convenient. For starters, Safari now lets you set up alerts for webpage changes, so you don't have to check yourself. This is useful if you're tracking a product's price, waiting for tickets to go on sale or keeping an eye on when an out-of-stock item becomes available again.
On your iPhone, launch Safari , head to a webpage you want to track, tap on the icon with three horizontal lines in the address bar and select Notify Me . Since this feature uses Apple Intelligence, you can describe what exactly you want Safari to monitor. You can then choose how frequently Safari checks the webpage for changes.

articles.title_orig: How To Use Your Phone To Find Hidden Cameras
articles.title_zh: How To Use Your Phone To Find Hidden Cameras
articles.content_orig:
When you feel wary, a quick check might provide some peace of mind.
For those of us who travel often, staying in a new location carries an unsettling risk: Airbnbs, hotels and other lodgings may have hidden cameras to spy on visitors. Short-term and privately owned rentals are of particular concern. While the full scale of the issue is unknown, a 2024 report from CNN found that Airbnb processed 35,000 support tickets related to "surveillance devices" in the preceding decade. While doorbell and outdoor security cameras have become increasingly common and are permitted under Airbnb rules, any indoor recording devices are banned from properties hosted on the platform.
The problem remains relatively uncommon. Airbnb said at the time of the CNN report that less than 0.1 percent of its properties were hit with safety complaints, including those related to security cameras. However, 51 percent of visitors said they don't trust short-term rentals, and such fears are not unfounded. Cameras are increasingly difficult to spot, often disguised as common home items like smoke detectors, chargers or picture frames. So it can sometimes be worth a check to ensure there are no surveillance devices in your lodging to ease your mind. But how do you find hidden cameras?
Your cell phone is a great tool to check for hidden cameras. Start with a simple flashlight sweep: close the curtains, turn off the lights, and then sweep the unit with a flashlight to check for any glimmering signs of electronics — the shine of a lens, or an LED light. Common places to hide cameras include smoke detectors, air purifiers, televisions, shower heads, or lights. Be particularly careful to check sensitive locations like near the bed or the shower. Mirrors are also important to check. If you shine a flashlight at a mirror, it should bounce back rather than passing through like a window. You can also put a finger directly onto a mirror. A real mirror will have a space between your finger and its reflection, while a two-way mirror will make it appear as though they are directly touching.
You can also use your phone camera to check for night-vision cameras in the room. These cameras emit infrared light, which on your camera app should appear as purple or white dots. To verify your phone can detect infrared light, point it at a TV remote control , push the buttons, and see if light coming from the remote can be detected. It is more likely your front-facing, or selfie camera, has this ability, but try using both to take a look. Once confirmed, you can scan the room with your phone to find IR emissions.
Many hidden cameras stream over Wi-Fi, and some mobile apps allow you to scan the network for unfamiliar devices. Options include Fing , Net Analyzer and WiFiman. Download a scanner app, connect to the Wi-Fi and search for names that you don't recognize — which will often include "cam" or "camera" to denote a recording device. Other names may map to common camera brands, like Wyze, Blink or TP-Link. Apps like Fing will show MAC addresses and device types, allowing you to further investigate names that show up in a scan. This is not always a straightforward method, however. Some devices like printers, televisions or other benign connected appliances are also likely to show up in such scans.
What's more, other devices may run their own networks, so check your phone's list of available Wi-Fi networks for similar, camera-related titles. Other cameras may use Bluetooth to connect, so a Bluetooth scan may also be helpful. To do this, you don't necessarily need a scanner app. You can just open your Bluetooth connections on the device and see what shows up.
These methods are not foolproof. Many cameras record to local memory cards, which means they won't show up on any kind of scan. Still, pairing this method with the flashlight sweep and the infrared light check is the most thorough way to check for surveillance.
If you think you have found a surveillance device in your lodging, be sure to double check using both the physical sweep method and digital scan. Once you have confirmed, do not touch the device: photograph it, reach out to the police and notify customer support for the platform you are using. Airbnb has clear policies against indoor cameras, even those that are not connected , and has in several reported cases removed hosts from the platform permanently and fully refunded guests who report such devices.
Vrbo also bans recording devices outright, and suggests guests who discover one report the incident immediately to the platform. Vrbo's policy states affected guests may be eligible for a refund. The CNN report regarding hidden cameras at Airbnb found there is no strict policy guiding employees to contact law enforcement in such incidents, so it's best to contact police yourself if you feel unsafe. Ultimately, a scan with your phone's flashlight, an infrared check with a camera and a sweep with a dedicated app can give you increased peace of mind when staying in an unfamiliar location.

articles.title_orig: Safari update brings vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, AI integration
articles.title_zh: Safari update brings vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, AI integration
articles.content_orig:
Safari is getting some major feature updates in the 27.3 updates to Apple’s operating systems, which are due in December and are appearing in a developer beta today: vertical tabs, an adaptive dark mode, and additional integration points with Siri AI.
In recent years, numerous browsers have experimented with re-orienting the traditional top-of-the-page tab bar into a vertical stack, and now Safari is joining the parade. (It makes sense, when you think about it, because most of our screens are much wider than they are tall, putting vertical space at a premium. 1 )
Vertical tabs aren’t a default, but they are now a new option. The tabs sit on the left sidebar as a strip of icons by default, but if you prefer you can resize the tab bar to also show tab titles. On the Mac, Apple has built a hover effect reminiscent of the macOS Dock that displays the name of the tab when you move the pointer over its icon, and if you pause and hover, it’ll display a floating window with a visual page preview.
Just as with the horizontal tab bar, you can pin tabs—in this case, by dragging them up to the top of the bar. And the new vertical tab system works with both Tab Groups and Apple Intelligence-organized topic views.
This feature isn’t just Mac-specific—it’s also available on iPad and on iPhone Duo, in both portrait and landscape. It’s configurable via the View menu on the Mac and the iPad, and in the Settings app on all platforms.
Apple added support for dark mode back in 2018, and web standards have supported the idea of an alternate dark appearance for ages. The problem is, and has always been, that if a website doesn’t explicitly support dark mode, it will blast its lightness into your eyes and make you unhappy. This is so frustrating that numerous extensions have been built to let users force websites into dark mode, my favorite of which has been Noir .
Still, it’s long past time for the Sherlocking of Noir, and here it comes. In 27.3, if Safari comes across a web page that doesn’t offer a dark mode, it has the ability to intelligently build a dark style for that site, not only darkening backgrounds but tuning text contrast, inverting some logos and graphics, recoloring vector artwork, lifting raised surfaces, and rebalancing layered shadows.
It’s an opt-in feature. When you encounter a site that could be darkened, Safari will ask you to try it out and see if you like it. You can opt to tell Safari to apply dark mode to all websites automatically, or approve the changes on a site-by-site basis.
If a site does offer a dark mode—but it’s one that may be a bit too light for comfort—well, Safari is going to respect the original designer’s wishes in that context. Basically, web designers who hate the idea of dark mode and have explicitly guarded against it will not be overridden by Safari. (See, there’s still at least one use case for third-party extensions!)
This is a great feature that’s long overdue as a part of Safari. But Apple needs to not stop here: HTML email in Apple Mail is also a disaster in dark mode. Also, this change doesn’t affect in-app WebViews today, which means your in-app browser sheet will still shout at you in the dark. Once this shakedown cruise in Safari is done, Apple needs to put these smarts everywhere.
Apple’s also expanding the ability for Siri AI to access the contents of web pages currently loaded in Safari. This new set of custom actions lets Safari understand the complete web content of all open tabs. (Currently it can just look at what’s displayed on screen.)
So for example, you could ask about content that’s way down on a page you’re looking at. Currently Safari can’t answer if it can’t see it, but in 27.3 it’ll be able to parse the entire page and find the answer.
Siri AI can also now take direct actions on your Safari tabs and windows, including moving, sorting, and organizing them. So you could ask Siri AI to put all your cooking tabs in a tab group, or sort a bunch of Amazon product pages by price, or close all those Amazon tabs. You can also add items to the Reading List and even ask Safari to clear your history, including per site.
These new features all appear in iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3. The first developer betas are now available, the public betas should be available in the next few weeks, and Apple expects 27.3 final to ship to everyone in December.

articles.title_orig: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.title_zh: What the midterm elections could mean for markets, debt
articles.content_orig:
‘Varney & Co.’ host Stuart Varney examines a potential socialist surge, Republican upsets in red states and what an election shakeup could mean for Congress and Wall Street.
Voters across America are casting their ballots in the midterm elections on Tuesday, which will determine control of Congress and could add to investors' concerns about oversight of the artificial intelligence (AI) sector and how the debt ceiling will be addressed next year.
Since President Donald Trump's second term began in 2025 with Republican majorities in both chambers of Congress, the S&P 500 has gained about 27% in part due to a massive influx of spending on AI and strong earnings growth.
Treasury yields are also significantly higher in part because of geopolitical risks that emerged with the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, which caused a surge in energy prices. U.S. budget deficits have continued to widen to about $2 trillion, adding more upward pressure to yields as debt issuance mounts.
Investors are weighing how the results of the election will affect the outlook for financial markets depending on whether Democrats take control of one or both chambers of Congress.
AFFORDABILITY TAKES CENTER STAGE AS AMERICANS CAST THEIR BALLOTS IN HIGH-STAKES MIDTERMS
The midterm elections will determine control of Congress for the next two years, carrying implications for the nation's finances and markets. (J. David Ake/Getty Images)
Since 1930, there have been eight midterm cycles when the president's party lost control of the House, and the S&P 500 rose for the remainder of the year five times, Ned Davis Research said. It posted a median gain of 1.4% from Election Day through year-end, slightly less than the 1.9% posted across all post-Election Day midterm years.
In a scenario in which Democrats win control of both chambers of Congress , investors expect tougher oversight of AI which could weigh on markets that have been pushed higher by the emerging tech.
Democratic majorities would have the ability to investigate corporate America while attempting to slow deregulation , which could increase market volatility.
DSA PLATFORM COULD COST UP TO $212T OVER A DECADE, ANALYSIS FINDS
Markets have generally fared well under divided government. (Michael Nagle/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
If Democrats win the House but Republicans hold their majority in the Senate, implications for the U.S. fiscal situation could be mixed.
Bipartisan compromises would be required over issues like funding the government to avoid shutdowns and raising the debt ceiling , which could create the potential for brinkmanship.
In a scenario where Republicans retain their majorities in the House and Senate, the GOP could pursue further tax reforms or boost defense spending.
FEDERAL BUDGET DEFICIT HITS $2T AS NATIONAL DEBT COSTS SURGE
The results of the midterms will impact negotiations between Congress and the Trump administration depending on who controls the House and Senate. (Grant Baldwin/AFP via Getty Images)
Ned Davis chief U.S. strategist Ed Clissold said that a House takeover by Democrats could modestly temper the U.S. equity market's year-end rally, but in general it hasn't prevented stocks from advancing.
"Conventional wisdom is that gridlock is good (for stocks)," said Clissold, adding that stocks have performed better under Democratic presidents than Republicans.
Diego Barnuevo, market analyst at Ebury, said that a Democratic-held Congress' negotiations with the White House would likely be limited to the budget and debt ceiling, and that a "Democratic sweep would be neutral to mildly positive for the fiscal outlook."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
A Republican sweep could ease concerns over investigations into AI companies that carry the potential to rattle markets.
"If Republicans maintain control of Congress, that would likely provide the most supportive incremental federal policy backdrop for the AI/infrastructure buildout through policy continuity, potential fiscal expansion, deregulation and faster federal permitting," JPMorgan strategists said in a note.
Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
articles.title_zh: Google to shut off search for schools that opt out of AI
articles.content_orig:
Google announced Tuesday morning that it would switch off AI products by default for students in schools that use the technology giant’s education software. But those schools that forgo its AI services would also be cut off from Google Search.
The move comes after mounting criticism from advocacy groups and senators about the spread of Google’s AI services available in classrooms. Until Tuesday, its AI products — branded under the Gemini moniker — were automatically activated for schools using Google Classroom.
Google said Tuesday’s move would also cut off students’ access to Google Search if schools do not enable Gemini, given AI’s growing integration into the company’s search products.
Chris Phillips, Google’s vice president and general manager of education, said in a blog post announcing the change that access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search “will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.”
“We believe schools should have control over AI in their classrooms and in providing administrators with controls to help them manage their approach,” Phillips wrote.
Some education and technology advocates immediately slammed the decision, painting the move as a punishment for schools that don’t use Google’s AI. “It is unfortunate that Google has prioritized its business interests over the education of our children,” said Randi Weingarten, president of the American Federation of Teachers, a national educators union.
“Instead of working with teachers and parents to uphold privacy and ensure their tools are safe and useful, it throws the baby out with the bathwater and bans access to the tools altogether,” she told NBC News in written comments.
Josh Golin, executive director of advocacy group Fairplay, said in a statement that Google is attempting “to strong-arm schools into using its AI products.”
“Schools should use this opportunity to help students find more privacy-protective alternatives for search, as well as ways to do more substantive research beyond search and click,” Golin said.
In a statement posted to social media after this article was published, Google said the announcements “give schools more choice, not less,” and that schools can turn on Google Search individually without enabling Gemini products. But Search will still have AI features built into it, which the company said have been updated “to make it better for learning. Specifically, AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.”
Earlier this year, Google turned on Gemini in its Classroom app, allowing children — regardless of age — to access AI products unless districts disabled it .
Parent advocacy groups and experts on the use of technology in schools denounced Google for providing AI products to children — raising concern that students would outsource their work to AI systems on school devices — and lobbied school districts to disable Gemini products. In an open letter in early October, 13 leading parent advocacy organizations — including the Digital Childhood Institute and Schools Beyond Screens — called on school districts to turn off access to Gemini and YouTube, which is also owned by Google .
Google has established a dominant role in education technology over the past 15 years. The vast majority of Chromebook laptops are purchased by school districts to provide to students. Nearly two-thirds of assignments use a Google product, according to a 2023 report by the firm Schoolytics. This year, the company began offering multiday AI trainings for educators, featuring sessions that focused on how they could mitigate pushback by teachers who don’t want to use AI.
Research on AI in educational settings has not established a long-term benefit for students. There are no high-quality causal studies into student use of AI, according to the SCALE Initiative at the Stanford Graduate School of Education . Researchers have also warned that many of the studies conducted so far on AI in education didn’t measure whether it boosted learning and often did not test whether AI-assisted learning was superior to other teaching methods.
In Tuesday’s blog post , Google said that for schools that enable the company’s AI products, they will now detect when a student is trying to use them just to get an answer on an assignment. A redesigned version of Google Search will instead walk students through the topic or problem and work through the concepts, without going directly to the answer, the company said.
Jared Perlo is a technology reporter focused on AI for NBC News Digital.
Tyler Kingkade is a national reporter for NBC News, based in Los Angeles.

articles.title_orig: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.title_zh: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search
articles.content_orig:
Senior Correspondent covering technology and culture
OpenAI is coming for Google Search, and it's working.
"ChatGPT's volume of search-like queries is now roughly one-fifth the volume of queries of Google," Adam Fry, ChatGPT's consumer product lead, told Alex Kantrowitz of the Big Technology newsletter.
It's good news for OpenAI. For Google? Not so great. It not only shows that people are willing to use AI, but that people were really, really, fed up with Google search results.
We already knew that basic information searching is currently the top use of LLMs like ChatGPT. Pew Research Center released a report this summer that showed that the top use case was to "search for information," with 42% of American adults surveyed saying they have used AI for that.
("For tasks at work" was the second most common use, with 38% of employed adults reporting that. Lesser uses include entertainment, getting news, and medical advice.)
This survey wasn't specifically about ChatGPT, but it's by far the most popular AI chatbot (44% of American adults surveyed told Pew they've used ChatGPT, and only 24% have used Gemini, the next most common).
ChatGPT now has 1.2 billion weekly users. We don't know how many of those users are doing informational searches as opposed to other things like coding or generating images, but it seems likely that someone who uses it to make images or chat would also ask it for information.
Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the competition from ChatGPT, but last year Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai addressed the issue during an interview with Bloomberg's Emily Chang.
"You've had these chatbots scale up to hundreds of millions of users. We've grown in queries," Pichai said at the time. "So I think it feels very far from a zero-sum game to me. To use another parallel, TikTok came in, everybody started using TikTok. YouTube grew and did very, very well in those moments too."
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Google says that it handles 5 trillion searches per year; it's dominated search for two decades, and very profitably!
But many people were getting really sick of Google search. So often in the last few years, I've heard friends or other people complain how Google search feels broken . Search results were so stuffed with SEO-friendly links that it often felt hard to trust anything or find the results you actually were searching for.
Users had started to add the term "Reddit" at the end of searches in hopes of getting better results — which ended up being a boon in traffic for Reddit (sadly, this didn't last; Reddit just reported a drop in search referral traffic due to Google's AI Overviews that it doesn't expect to get back).
So when ChatGPT came along, suddenly there was a new way to get information and answers without all the SEO fluff — and plenty of people were thrilled. Sure, the information isn't always reliable. Everyone should know better than to blindly trust facts doled out by AI, which is prone to hallucinations or just plain bungling, like telling people to put glue in their pizza .
Despite the issues with trusting AI for information (and to be fair, it has improved since the glue/pizza fiasco of 2024), it's clear that tons of people were very, very happy to switch over to ChatGPT instead of Google for their informational searching needs.
I think what we should consider is that says a lot more about how bad Google had gotten than it does about how good ChatGPT is. There's a compelling case to be made that Google enshittified its flagship product so badly — perhaps from the years and years of having no meaningful competitors — that it was a sitting duck, ready to have its lunch eaten by the first new disruptor to come along and offer people a better way.
Google eventually realized it was in trouble, issuing a "code red" in 2022 over ChatGPT. It might be time to issue another one?

articles.title_orig: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.title_zh: NYT demands Brave shut down its paywall blocker and end deals with AI firms
articles.content_orig:
The New York Times and other newspaper companies sued Brave Software yesterday, alleging that the browser maker illegally bypasses paywalls and sells stolen news content to AI companies.
“Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere,” the NYT alleged in a lawsuit filed in US District Court for the Southern District of New York. Citing third-party revenue estimates, the suit claimed that “Brave has made more than $100 million by copying and reselling publishers’ work without consent or permission,” while “publishers have received nothing.”
The lawsuit said, “AI companies pay Brave to provide them with real-time online content from the Brave search index,” and use content from the Brave index “to train their own AI models” and “to respond to specific user queries.” The NYT lawsuit points to Brave’s website , which says the Brave Search API is “used by some of the biggest names in AI, including Cohere, Mistral, Perplexity, and You.com.”
The lawsuit accused Brave of all the major types of copyright infringement: direct infringement, contributory infringement, and vicarious infringement. The lawsuit claims Brave infringes copyrights directly by scraping articles for its search index, for its “Ask Brave” AI search feature, and for the Brave API that “serves as an illicit source of unlicensed copyrighted material, including Times journalism, to other AI companies.”
The NYT accused Brave of being “a contributory and vicarious infringer when it deliberately induces, facilitates, controls, and profits from its users’ and GenAI customers’ copying of the copyrighted content.” Finally, the lawsuit said Brave violated the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) by circumventing technological measures the NYT and other content owners use to restrict access to their articles.
“The Brave Browser includes a default setting that, when activated, causes the browser to go behind website paywalls and provide the paywalled content to the user,” the lawsuit said. The browser “blocks advertising that would otherwise appear on The Times’s website, and instead shows its own ads, offering its users a cut of the revenue even as it deprives The Times of digital advertising revenue that helps it fund the expensive effort of producing journalism,” the lawsuit said.
When testing the Brave browser for Mac today, we found that the optional “paywall blocker” feature made it possible to read a paywalled New York Times article. The feature was enabled in the default settings and can be turned off.
The NYT asked for a permanent injunction to stop Brave from continuing the allegedly illegal conduct. The lawsuit seeks statutory damages, actual damages, restitution of profits derived from alleged copyright infringement, and “restitution and disgorgement of all revenue and profits Brave obtained through its ad-substitution scheme.”
A similar lawsuit was filed against Brave in the same court yesterday by the New York Daily News, Chicago Tribune, and Orlando Sentinel companies. We contacted Brave and will update this article if it provides a response.
Perplexity, which is not a defendant in the Brave lawsuit but is facing a different lawsuit filed by the NYT, accused the news organization of “disinformation” in a statement provided to Ars and other news outlets. Perplexity’s statement did not identify any specific inaccuracies in the lawsuit against Brave.
“The New York Times is overpaying its attorneys and underpaying its journalists. (Who could’ve easily identified the disinformation in this suit.),” Perplexity’s statement said.
The NYT sued Perplexity in December 2025, alleging that its AI tool gives users “outputs that are identical or substantially similar to” NYT articles, including “verbatim or near-verbatim reproductions, summaries, or abridgements of the original content.” Perplexity’s response to that lawsuit said its answer engine only fetches content from copyrighted articles in reply to user queries. Perplexity argued that “developing an AI tool that can allegedly automatically fetch and provide specific content in response to user requests based on its pre-configuration and access to materials available on the Internet” is not “volitional conduct.”
The NYT also sued OpenAI and Microsoft in December 2023 in a lawsuit alleging that OpenAI trains its AI with stolen news content. The lawsuit is heading toward a trial , with OpenAI arguing that its use of news articles is fair use under copyright law.

articles.title_orig: US Stocks Waver as Election, AI Bubble Risks Weigh on Outlook
articles.title_zh: US Stocks Waver as Election, AI Bubble Risks Weigh on Outlook
articles.content_orig:
Buckle up for another wild week in markets.
Investors are still coming off a roller coaster ride that included a painful sell-off in the AI trade on Friday, but the volatility isn't expected to die down soon, and a handful of potential catalysts is lies ahead for investors.
This week's docket includes more Big Tech earnings , economic data updates, and the midterm elections, which have historically been a hurdle for markets to clear.
And then there's the fragile state of the AI trade, which was rattled last week as concerns about capex and overall AI demand rocked the market. The Nasdaq 100 , which logged its worst month in over a year, is now on the edge of entering an official correction, with the tech-heavy index down 9% from its high in early October.
Here's what investors are facing next:
Apple , the largest company in the world by market cap after Nvidia's plunge last Friday, is on deck to report results for the third quarter after the bell on Monday, a marquee event that's expected to shape sentiment in the tech trade after last week's sell-off. Here's what Wall Street is expecting from the iPhone maker:
Investors will be paying special attention to the firm's comments on AI. Apple isn't a capex story the same way companies like Meta and Microsoft are. Its spending is expected to come in at around $11 billion to $14 billion this year, compared to the $100+ billion from AI hyperscalers, but the market remains eager to see what the iPhone maker's AI ambitions will look like in the post-Tim Cook era. The coming earnings call will be the first to be led by new CEO John Ternus , setting the tone for the tech giant's new chapter.
The market has been mercurial on Big Tech earnings lately, with investors ready to punish big AI firms at any whiff of bad news. Meta and Tesla were negatively impacted after reporting third-quarter results that hinted at slight changes in spending outlooks, triggering fears that slowing investment could spark a wave of knock-on effects for other suppliers in the industry.
Amazon and Alphabet, on the other hand, spooked investors by suggesting capex would grow next year despite negative cash flow, leading the market to punish those tech giants for what it saw as excessive spending.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Palantir , another notable player in the AI universe, will also report earnings after the bell.
"We continue to evaluate the monetization versus spending conundrum for hyperscalers," Eric Freedman, the CIO at Northern Trust, wrote in a note on Monday. "While results were very company-specific, the common threads markets focus on are capital expenditure plans, financing needs, existing business cannibalization and evidence of returns."
Oil is an enduring story in markets in 2026, one that's sparked major bouts of volatility in both stocks and bonds. On Monday, Brent and West Texas Intermediate crude eacg dropped 6% as investors took in the possibility that the US and Iran could revive attempts at a diplomatic resolution to the war.
State Secretary Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump preferred to wrap up the conflict with Iran "peacefully," adding that the president hasn't yet decided to attack Iran.
However, more volatility could be looming.
Oil prices spiked in recent weeks on a New York Times report that the US and Israel are drawing up plans to strike Iran after the midterm elections. Energy markets could see more volatility this week if the market sees fresh signs evidence that peace talks are progressing or the administration signals that strikes will resume.
After months of anticipation, the midterm elections are finally here.
Wall Street is eyeing the passing of the midterm elections as a potential catalyst for markets. Stocks have historically struggled into the midterms, but have seen strong gains in the months following, with the S&P 500 gaining an average of 14% in the six months after the midterms since 1970, according to an analysis from BlackRock.
JPMorgan Private Bank said it was eyeing "outsized" gains in the S&P 500 , pointing to improved market breadth, or the measure of winning stocks to losing stocks, in the overall index lately. The bank also recently lifted its year-end price target for the S&P 500 to 8,000, implying 4% upside from the index's current levels.
The bank's market intelligence team flagged near-term volatility depending on the results of the election and outlined the possible reaction in stocks depending on each election outcome.
S&P 500 drops as much as 25 basis points or gains as much as 50 basis points.
Some investors fear an "AI sell-off" in the event of a Democratic sweep, but in that scenario, any pullback in markets would be an "opportunity to buy the dip," strategists wrote in a note.
"SPX has been up a year after every midterm election since 1950 with an average gain of around 15%," the bank's Craig Cohen wrote in a client note. "I suspect that at least part of the reason for this tendency is that the midterms tend to see the incumbent party loses seats and gridlock in Washington tends to be good for Wall Street."
" Volatility could stay up awaiting results. Typically, stocks rally after midterms, but one exception was 2018—also a rate hike year," Joe Mazzola, a head trading and derivatives strategist at Charles Schwab, wrote in a note.
Finally, investors will get a major macroeconomic update in the October jobs report on Friday. It's a data point that could shape the Fed's projected path for interest rate hikes through the rest of this year and early next year.
Central bankers left rates unchanged at their last policy meeting , as expected, pointing to the need to assess the trajectory of inflation before moving rates further. Markets, though, are expecting a rate hike at the Fed's next policy meeting, with the probability of a 25 basis-point rate increase rising to 78% on Monday, according to CME FedWatch.
A strong jobs report, while good news for the economy, risks creating a reason for investors to sell stocks. The logic is that a stronger job market reflects the economy's capacity to absorb higher interest rates, a possible drag for risk assets.
Economists are expecting the US to have added 55,000 payrolls last month, up from the 29,000 jobs added in September.

articles.title_orig: Germany’s Merz warns Europe needs seat at the table as Trump renews Ukraine talks
articles.title_zh: Germany’s Merz warns Europe needs seat at the table as Trump renews Ukraine talks
articles.content_orig:
Russia on Tuesday confirmed that peace talks with Ukraine and the U.S. will go ahead next week in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, while also signaling that a meeting between Presidents Vladimir Putin , Donald Trump and Xi Jinping to end the conflict was on the table.
Putin aide Vladimir ​Medinsky will serve ⁠as Moscow's chief negotiator ​at the talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, Kremlin spokesman ​Dmitry Peskov told reporters on a conference call, according to Reuters.
Separately, first lady Melania Trump will bring Russian and Ukrainian representatives to the White House to discuss the local ceasefire in Kherson, the White House said Tuesday.
Monday saw the end of a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and surrounding areas in the Kherson region to allow for evacuation of residents, in a pause of hostilities that the White House said was brokered by the first lady.
Ukraine on Monday accused Russia of using the ceasefire to reinforce its military positions in the city.
The first lady's summit on Thursday will be "an extraordinary moment in American history," the White House said, but did not name the representatives who will attend. Melania Trump will deliver remarks on the Oleshky ceasefire at 11 a.m. ET on Thursday, it added.
Peskov also said Tuesday the Kremlin hopes to finalize plans for a trilateral meeting between the leaders of Russia, the U.S. and China in the coming days. The comments follow earlier reports that these countries were planning to negotiate an end to the war in Ukraine, without Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the table.
Zelenskyy has said that any negotiations over Ukraine's future must include Kyiv.
"It can be acceptable only when we are at the table of negotiations," he said on Oct. 20, adding that he had discussed the proposal of a three-way meeting between the U.S., China and Russia to negotiate an end to the nearly five-year full-scale war. "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine," he said.
Tensions between the U.S. and Ukraine have mounted over recent weeks amid continued strikes between Moscow and Kyiv, including on civilian and energy targets.
A series of moves by the Trump administration in October raised questions about Washington's reliability as Kyiv's most important military partner.
Tuesday's announcement follows U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff saying late Monday that Washington will mediate Ukraine-Russia peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, focusing on security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues.
Witkoff also said that U.S. negotiators will meet European and NATO officials in Brussels this week to discuss postwar security guarantees and Ukraine's reconstruction.

articles.title_orig: China’s HQ-9B air defense system destroys maneuvering missile in tests
articles.title_zh: China’s HQ-9B air defense system destroys maneuvering missile in tests
articles.content_orig:
Authorities in Beijing announced that the PLA Air Force utilized the HQ-9B surface-to-air missile platform to successfully neutralize targets during a training drill. These objectives consisted of missiles capable of rapid movement and complex maneuvering.
The evaluations of the HQ-9B, a modern addition to the Chinese military inventory, required the interception of two distinct missile varieties. One specific target executed an abrupt mid-air pivot before plummeting toward the earth at extreme velocity.
According to the state media outlet China Central Television (CCTV), the Central Theater Command's Shenwei Missile Battalion within the PLA Air Force carried out the maneuvers.
Personnel from the Shenwei Missile Battalion were not briefed on the specific nature of the incoming threats; they were informed only that the mission involved engaging agile, high-velocity projectiles.
A battalion participant noted that the crew was afforded a mere two-second window to react. In this brief interval, they were required to identify the mysterious object and determine if a launch was necessary.
Military specialist Song Zhongping remarked, in a report by the Global Times , that despite precise radar monitoring, a defense system must possess the capacity for mid-flight trajectory adjustments to successfully follow a target exhibiting erratic flight patterns.
For guidance and tracking during an engagement, the HQ-9B utilizes an active radar homing (ARH) mechanism paired with an inertial navigation system (INS). Beyond its sophisticated steering and engine technologies, the HQ-9B is capable of striking targets that follow non-linear flight paths. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of a missile intercept is contingent upon multiple variables, such as communication reliability, target velocity, reaction speed, and radar precision.
The drill also showcased the PLA's ability to fuse different missile, command, and radar elements into a cohesive air defense web. Expert Song Zhongping clarified that China has established a unified data-sharing architecture for its diverse air defense branches to distribute intelligence on approaching hazards and synchronize their actions. Threats are distributed among various units depending on their proximity and combat readiness.
Hu Yang, another member of the battalion, mentioned that just two minutes elapse between the reception of a high-level warning and the actual interception. While the drill proves the HQ-9B can hit maneuvering missiles, its capacity to stop hypersonic cruise missiles or glide vehicles requires separate validation through authentic combat simulations.
Although the HQ-9B might intercept a target approaching directly, engaging hypersonic cruise missiles or glide vehicles presents an extreme challenge for any surface-to-air hardware. Testing the HQ-9B against maneuvering aerial targets does not verify its effectiveness against operational hypersonic technology. Assessing the system's utility against such weaponry would require distinct trials in practical operational settings.
Earlier, during September 2025, China exhibited numerous air defense assets . Featured hardware included the HQ-29, HQ-19, HQ-9C, and HQ-9B. These platforms represent China's expanding proficiency in defending against diverse missile types and fixed-wing aircraft.
The latest HQ-9B drills highlight the ongoing technical advancement of China's armed forces. Still, the ability of the system to negate sophisticated missile hazards remains unproven until subjected to independent testing in lifelike combat scenarios.

articles.title_orig: Itch mass deletes ‘AI slop’, lets users filter out any AI assisted games
articles.title_zh: Itch mass deletes ‘AI slop’, lets users filter out any AI assisted games
articles.content_orig:
The indie video game store that prides itself as an open marketplace is being deluged by game pages, doubling the usual number without a proportional increase in sales.
Itch.io, a small independent game distribution store that allows any and all game creators to sell their games, reports that the number of store pages for games has doubled per-day in the past two months. In a post on Bluesky , a site representative implied this unprecedented rise is due to to generative AI's effects on game development, but points out that the increase in the number of pages has not resulted in a commensurate rise in sales or revenue.
The Bluesky post post reads "The number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past 2 months," accompanied by an image of a chart that shows a raise from 3,000 pages created on a given day around August to nearly 8,000 pages in October. While the Itch.io post does not directly say that this is because of generative AI, multiple replies to the post from other users ask if that is the case, and the Itch.io account responds with either tired emojis or robots.
Related: Valve weighs in on Next Fest AI cloning phenomenon
A further reply also clarifies that "the number of downloads and purchases has *not* doubled," indicating that the higher number of game pages doesn't seem to be benefitting the store or developers in any significant way.
Browsing Itch.io's page of newest games , which shows games in the latest order they have been added, one can observe numerous thumbnails made using generative AI. Filtering using the "No AI" button removes entire pages from the store listings, going from 1,772,099 results down to 432,180 results. The AI disclosure tag is applied when a creator adds a game page, asking if the game contains any generative AI in the assets, but does not require the question to be answered for a page to be created.
In the Itch.io content creator quality guidelines, the section on generative AI includes a plea for truthful disclosure. "We ask that you accurately tag your project if it contains materials produced by generative AI by utilizing the AI Disclosure section on your project’s edit page." The overall guidelines page does say that failure to adhere to the guidelines could result in a page being removed, but it is unclear what the processes are for a game being removed for containing generative AI without reporting it.
Itch.io isn't the only video game storefront to see a rise in dashed-off AI games. In response to the flood of AI copies on its own store, Valve has asked developers on Steam to make their games "less likely to be copied" and to encourage developers to stand out by using Steam's community features to their fullest extent.
Imran Khan has been in the games industry in various forms for over two decades. He has been a former senior editor at Game Informer, a professional loudmouth at Kinda Funny, and news director at Fanbyte. He has also been doing PR for Vicarious PR and Head of U.S. PR for Japanese VR studio MyDearest, in addition to Producer work on their latest title Brazen Blaze.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine's rescuers deal with grim aftermath of aid shelter bombings as Moscow pounds energy targets
articles.title_zh: Ukraine's rescuers deal with grim aftermath of aid shelter bombings as Moscow pounds energy targets
articles.content_orig:
Other overnight strikes targeted power plants across Ukraine, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people
Russia has bombed a humanitarian hub in southern Ukraine , killing at least 31 people and leaving dozens missing, as part of a wave of strikes across the country.
Other overnight Russian strikes targeted power plants across Ukraine, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people, as the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, warned that the US was distracted by its midterm elections.
In total, Russia had launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, Zelenskyy said in an online post.
“The Russians think America won’t notice this signal of theirs,” he said. “But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes,” he said.
The barrage came just a day after a rare local ceasefire in neighbouring Kherson ended, underscoring the limits of the temporary truce.
The deadliest guided-bomb attack first targeted a school building used to distribute humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, a village in Ukraine’s southern Zaporizhzhia region, and then took aim at a nearby shelter.
The dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, Mykhailo Semikin, the acting head of the regional military administration, said on Tuesday. At least five people were hurt. Semikin said 48 people were considered missing.
As night fell in Komyshuvakha, emergency responders used torches to search through the rubble of collapsed buildings, according to photos and video posted online by local officials.
Efforts to rescue people on Monday evening were hindered as Russian drones launched additional attacks in the area that had been bombed, according to Mykhailo Semikin, a military official in Zaporizhzhia.
Zelenskyy said the Russians could not have been unaware that residents remaining in Komyshuvakha gathered each week to pick up humanitarian packages from the site.
The attack, he said, had shown that Moscow was intent on killing people instead of building on the past week’s ceasefire in the embattled southern city of Oleshky , brokered by the US first lady, Melania Trump.
“Russians continue to demonstrate, time and again, their hatred of Ukraine and everything that exists here,” Zelenskyy said.
In the north-east region of Kharkiv, a combined Russian missile and drone attack had wounded at least 62 people, local authorities said. A strike damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars. More than 200 patients had been transferred to other medical facilities, said the head of the regional military administration, Oleh Syniehubov.
“If Russia genuinely ‌wanted de-escalation, there was an opportunity following the situation in Oleshky to continue taking humanitarian steps. We proposed this. But Russia continues to kill people,” Zelenskyy said.
The ceasefire last week enabled an evacuation of the Russian-occupied Oleshky. It was the longest pause in fighting between the neighbours in the war, now in its fifth year, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.
The Kremlin said that no other similar missions were being planned “at the moment”.
US-led talks between Russia and Ukraine were due to resume next week, the US special envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday.
Donald Trump, who pledged during his election campaign to end the war in a single day, has repeatedly pushed for a settlement but has so far failed to secure a breakthrough.
The latest round of talks is scheduled for 10-11 November in Abu Dhabi, according to Witkoff, amid growing concerns in Kyiv and among its European allies over Trump’s increasingly close ties with Moscow and discussions of potential business deals between the US and Russia.
Russia announced on Tuesday that its delegation would be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a hardline former culture minister who has headed several previous rounds of negotiations with Ukraine.
Medinsky’s earlier appointment as chief negotiator was met with scepticism by Ukrainian officials and analysts, who questioned whether he had the authority to make meaningful concessions. A key architect of the historical revisionism used by Putin to justify his invasion of Ukraine, Medinsky has long promoted the Kremlin’s narrative that Ukraine is inseparable from Russia.
Zelenskyy, meanwhile, arrived in Berlin for talks with the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz. Germany has become Ukraine’s largest provider of military aid since Merz took office in May 2025, overtaking the US as American support has declined.
The Ukrainian president is also expected to attend this year’s Berlin Security Conference.
Reuters and Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title_orig: Israeli Claims of Iranian Chemical Weapons Divide U.S. Officials
articles.title_zh: Israeli Claims of Iranian Chemical Weapons Divide U.S. Officials
articles.content_orig:
Israel has provided the United States with intelligence indicating that Iran is considering using chemical weapons against its adversaries, but officials in Washington are divided over the information's credibility and significance, The New York Times reported on Tuesday, citing American and regional officials.
Some senior US officials received the intelligence with concern, while others expressed deep skepticism, viewing it as part of a pressure campaign by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government aimed at convincing the Trump administration to resume large-scale fighting against Iran .
According to the report, during discussions with US intelligence agencies and other officials over the past two weeks, senior Israeli officials presented the chemical weapons threat as more urgent than Iran's ambitions to develop nuclear weapons.
Israeli intelligence officials told their American counterparts that they believe Iran is rapidly advancing technology that would allow it to mount chemical weapons on missiles or smuggle them into Israel or another country to carry out an attack.
Other senior American officials believe the threat should be taken seriously, particularly in light of a series of recent warnings about Iranian preparations to attack US interests.
According to the newspaper, there is little disagreement within the American intelligence community that Iran is developing chemical weapons. The central dispute concerns whether Iranian leaders would actually use them, particularly if Iran is not attacked again.
Israel also shared some of the intelligence with officials in Gulf states. Several questioned whether Iran was developing plans to use chemical weapons and believe Israel is attempting to push the United States and its partners toward a more intensive phase of the war.
A regional official told the newspaper that Israel had presented Gulf countries with assessments suggesting Iran was working to make its chemical weapons operational, but had not shared supporting evidence.
According to the official, Gulf governments regarded the claims as lacking seriousness.
For some American officials, the warnings have revived memories of the faulty intelligence surrounding Iraq's weapons of mass destruction in 2002.
At the time, US intelligence agencies presented the White House with a firm assessment that Iraq possessed such weapons, although the country had largely abandoned or suspended its nuclear, chemical and biological weapons programs.
Even among those briefed on the new intelligence, assessments differ regarding how quickly and effectively Iran could deploy chemical weapons.
According to experts and American officials who spoke with the newspaper, mounting a chemical weapon on a ballistic missile is not particularly difficult, but ensuring the effective dispersal of the chemical agent is more complicated.
Smuggling a bomb across a border also presents difficulties. Another possibility mentioned was the use of a drone.
Despite the Israeli warnings, the newspaper reported that preparations for responding to chemical weapons attacks are not a central component of the Home Front Command exercises taking place across Israel this week.
Two Home Front Command officials said there had also been no widespread reminders distributed to officers or the public regarding protective instructions against such a threat.
The IDF declined to comment.
The intelligence was shared as the United States and Iran explore the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough while simultaneously preparing for a resumption of hostilities.
According to senior American officials, US Central Command (CENTCOM) has a plan for an attack on Iran that could be carried out as early as Wednesday, November 4, one day after the US midterm elections.
The report stated that three American aircraft carriers are currently in the region, while the preferred operational window for an attack is expected to be brief.
One of the aircraft carriers will need to return to its home port after the beginning of November, and particularly dark nights are expected in the coming days, providing favorable conditions for military operations.
However, President Donald Trump has not yet approved a large-scale attack, and diplomatic contacts between Washington and Tehran are continuing.
In recent weeks, the United States has concentrated warships, fighter jets and bombers in the region in preparation for a possible relatively short military campaign involving intensive strikes.
At the same time, diplomats are attempting to formulate an agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, address Iran's nuclear program and postpone further military action.
According to the report, the military buildup could also serve as leverage to support the diplomatic effort.
Meanwhile, US intelligence agencies assess that the threat to Americans in the Middle East and several other countries is at its highest level since the war began in February.
Intelligence collection was intensified after an Iranian plot to attack a base in Britain used by American fighter jets was uncovered.
On October 23, a warning memorandum regarding potential Iranian attacks was sent to senior administration officials. Diplomats and other personnel were subsequently placed on heightened alert.
The newspaper also linked Netanyahu's efforts to his political situation following the Israeli elections, in which he failed to secure a clear path toward forming a government.
Several commentators who spoke with the newspaper suggested that Netanyahu might attempt to use a national security emergency to pressure opposition leaders into joining a coalition under his leadership.
American allegations regarding an Iranian chemical weapons program date back decades.
In 2003, Iran acknowledged that it had developed chemical capabilities during the Iran-Iraq War but claimed that it subsequently dismantled them.
Tehran denies possessing chemical weapons and has previously described such accusations as psychological warfare conducted by Israel and Netanyahu .
Dana Stroul, a former senior Pentagon official responsible for Middle East policy during the Biden administration, said it has been known for more than two decades that Iran has been stockpiling components for chemical weapons, but has never used them.
However, she warned that Tehran could feel "existential pressure" and potentially cross the threshold into directly using such weapons offensively.
A spokesperson for Netanyahu's office told the NYT : "Israel closely monitors every threat posed by the Iranian terrorist regime and is prepared to confront it."
The White House did not respond to the newspaper's request for comment, but an American official said Trump would defend the United States and its allies against any potential threat.

articles.title_orig: US job postings jumped sharply in September, potentially a good sign for anyone seeking employment
articles.title_zh: US job postings jumped sharply in September, potentially a good sign for anyone seeking employment
articles.content_orig:
U.S. employers ramped up their job postings in September as stronger economic growth may be encouraging more hiring
WASHINGTON -- U.S. employers ramped up their job postings in September as stronger economic growth may be encouraging more hiring. Yet voters are headed to the polls Tuesday largely gloomy over an economy beset by higher prices .
U.S. job openings jumped to 7.5 million from a revised 7.19 million in August, the Labor Department reported Tuesday . It is the largest number of openings since May and up from a recent low of 6.9 million in March.
The department’s Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS) also showed that gross hiring — job gains before subtracting people who quit or lost jobs — rose and layoffs fell in September.
The increases are a hopeful sign that hiring could improve, but the trend would have to continue for several months to suggest real improvement. Hiring has been sluggish for nearly three years, though layoffs have also been historically low, a sign of meager “churn” in the labor market. Low churn means those who are employed are enjoying relatively high levels of job security, but it is much harder than normal for those looking for work to find a job.
The government will issue the October jobs report on Friday, which is forecast to show that employers added 65,000 positions last month, according to data provider FactSet. That would be an improvement from 29,000 in September. The unemployment rate is expected to stay at a low 4.2%.
Typically, job gains of just 65,000 would be seen as a sign of a struggling economy, but with the giant baby boom generation retiring and immigration sharply reduced , the economy doesn’t need to generate as many jobs as it has in the past for unemployment to remain low.
In September, layoffs fell sharply to just 1.64 million, the fewest since March 2025. The number of people quitting their jobs rose to 3.37 million, the highest in about 18 months, and up from 3.04 million.
The rise in quits is generally a good sign because workers usually leave a job when they either have another lined up or when they are confident they can find new work.

articles.title_orig: Why the Anthropic IPO 'could be the swing vote' for Wall Street bank stocks
articles.title_zh: Why the Anthropic IPO 'could be the swing vote' for Wall Street bank stocks
articles.content_orig:
The midterm elections could reshape Congress as lawmakers grapple with persistent inflation , high energy prices and rising fiscal debt . For investors, by contrast, the political outcome could deliver a boost.
Data from financial firm Edward Jones shows that the S&P 500 stock index rose an average of 1.7% in the month after the last 14 midterm races, dating back to 1970. In the six months following midterm elections, S&P returns averaged 15.5%.
"Volatility around the vote is possible, but markets have historically performed well in the year following midterms as political uncertainty recedes and attention returns to the economic outlook," Magdalena Ocampo, market strategist at the global investment firm Principal Asset Management, said in an email on Tuesday as Americans cast their votes.
With congressional control in the balance, Wall Street analysts are also considering the impact divided government could have on stocks if the Democrats win the House, Senate or both chambers. Political gridlock has historically been good for markets because it limits Congress' ability to pass sweeping tax and spending legislation, reducing the risk of volatility, according to analysts.
"Less change makes a more predictable environment, which allows companies to invest in longer-term projects," Chris Low, chief economist at FHN Financial, a capital markets firm, said in an email Tuesday. "That tends to be good for earnings."
Less stock market volatility doesn't guarantee investors an easy ride, however. Gridlock in Washington, D.C., could also fuel another partisan standoff on the nation's debt, which recently surpassed $40 trillion , or spur the U.S. government to increase its borrowing to fund its priorities, according to economists.
That could unnerve bond investors, who are worried that Washington is on an unsustainable fiscal trajectory, Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research, said in a note to investors.
"Prolonged shutdowns and fiscal standoffs could push Treasury yields higher, weighing on equity valuations," he said.
The Bipartisan Policy Center, a Washington, D.C.-based think tank, estimates that the U.S. will reach the debt limit again sometime between late winter and midsummer of 2027. At that point, lawmakers will have to decide whether to raise the debt ceiling, temporarily suspend it or risk another government shutdown.
Volatility could also persist if President Trump continues to rely on his executive authority to accomplish his priorities, Yardeni said. In that case, Democrats would have little power to restrain Mr. Trump even if they controlled Congress, he noted.
"Hence, a blue wave could deliver a cold shower for stocks, though we would view a significant selloff as a buying opportunity given the remarkable strength of the economy and corporate earnings," Yardeni said.
A Democratic sweep could have other implications for the economy beyond financial markets. That could include Democrats blocking Trump-appointed regulators, according to Jaret Seiberg, a financial policy analyst and managing director at investment bank TD Cowen.
"They [could] leverage this power to force the President to fill Democratic seats on independent agencies like the FDIC, SEC and CFTC," he said.
A Democratic majority in the Senate would also elevate Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, to head the Senate Banking Committee, giving her more latitude to pass populist legislation, Seiberg added. Warren would replace South Carolina Republican Sen. Tim Scott, who currently chairs the influential panel.

articles.title_orig: Google dismantles botnet secretly running on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
articles.title_zh: Google dismantles botnet secretly running on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
articles.content_orig:
Visibility and context on the threats that matter most.
Last week, Google and industry partners dismantled the XCPE backdoor which enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet. We assess with high confidence that the backdoor and botnet were intentionally developed, deployed, and operated for financial gain by Videostrong Technology Co., an Android Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) and Original Design Manufacturer (ODM).
Videostrong monetized the backdoor by selling access to criminal affiliates and loading those affiliates’ malware modules onto infected devices. These secondary modules were conducting ad-fraud; silently enrolling infected devices into residential proxy networks; and loading additional malware onto XCPE-compromised devices. We also took action to disrupt the command and control (C2) domains that operate these affiliate modules. Because these affiliates each have diversified distribution channels for their modules beyond XCPE, we assess that taking down their C2 domains will sever access to at least 10 million additional compromised devices.
We found this malicious software built directly into many different device models and brands over multiple years, supported by dedicated infrastructure and constantly evolving configurations to evade detection and manage their affiliates. We believe this campaign wasn’t an isolated rogue insider or a development oversight. As a result, Google has cut ties with Videostrong and banned them from making devices with preloaded Google apps.
Google requires OEMs go through a comprehensive suite of compatibility and security tests to ensure a consistent and safe user experience across the Android ecosystem. However, Videostrong employed obfuscation techniques to exploit a gap in our tests and load malicious code after the device's first boot. As a result, Google has implemented changes to its existing review process to better safeguard against similar activity in the future. A device manufacturer intentionally infecting their users with malware is an unacceptable breach of trust, and represents a serious risk to those users. Without users’ knowledge or consent, infected devices were offered as a distribution mechanism for a wide array of criminal actors. This led to a variety of malicious activities being conducted on and through the devices, including ad-fraud, data exfiltration, and routing malicious network traffic through the devices.
We worked closely with Japan’s National Police Agency, Lumen, HUMAN Security, Plume, Synthient, and TrendAI to analyze this malware ecosystem and disrupt its operations.
While we expect this disruption to have a significant effect on these criminal operations, this is not the end of our work combatting malicious activity. Backdoor operators, ad-fraud rings, and residential proxy providers operate as an interconnected supply chain. Point-in-time disruptions are a critical tool to protect our users, but  lasting disruption in this fluid ecosystem will require continued targeting of this infrastructure.
Google undertook the following actions to support disruption of the XCPE botnet:
Legal action to take down the domains and servers Videostrong used to control the botnet and install malware modules
Legal action to take down C2 domains used by over a dozen malware families loaded as modules via this backdoor
Banned Videostrong and any future subsidiaries or affiliates from building and selling certified Android devices in the future, or supplying software to other certified vendors
Implementing improvements to how we ensure the integrity of firmware on certified Android TV devices
The x.cpe network was built for ongoing profit. By giving malware affiliates backdoor access, the operators conspired to monetize these devices long after purchase.
Figure 1: XCPE malware overview
Since at least late 2024, Videostrong has evolved its pre-installed malware from simple single-stage droppers into a modular, three-stage architecture designed for resilience and multi-tenant monetization:
Primary Backdoor: Operating at the android.uid.system privilege level, x.cpe (running as com.oemservice in some builds) is preloaded in the firmware partition. If uninstalled by a user, it automatically reinstalls from the /oem/ partition upon reboot, maintaining persistent system-level access. Its main function is to establish and facilitate communications between the C2 server and the loader and execution engine.
Loader and Execution Engine: To evade security scans, x.cpe acts primarily as the C2 communicator and offloads module execution to an external loader, com.abc.nexus . This file employs native anti-analysis utilities to thwart sandbox detection, and configures and initializes the monetization modules. Most recently, com.abc.nexus has itself been phased out in favor of using more tailored dropper malware that loads and executes single modules.
Monetization Modules: Videostrong monetizes its backdoored devices by loading monetization modules which are developed by entities other than Videostrong that act as affiliates. These modules are deployed as native ELF daemons, embedded SDKs compiled directly into the com.abc.nexus DEX bytecode, or are fetched as secondary APKs from the malware staging infrastructure.  The loaded modules transform infected devices into residential proxy exit nodes (e.g., Linkfog, AppSalt, NetNut), ad-fraud engines (e.g., CBOXTV, HiddenView), or execute additional backdoors that load even more monetization modules (e.g. Moyu, Spirit).
Command and Control: The botnet uses a two-stage C2 process. It first initiates HTTP POST requests to fetch dynamic configuration settings, geolocation data, and STUN server parameters. It then establishes a persistent, real-time Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) connection to receive instructions for silent app installations, arbitrary shell commands, screen captures, and network reconnaissance. MQTT is a lightweight, publish-and-subscribe network protocol designed for low-bandwidth, high-latency, or unreliable remote networks.
The infection chain begins with a stub package (called x.cpe in some builds and com.oemservice in others) preloaded in the system partition of the firmware and running at the android.uid.system privilege level. This stub has limited functionality. Upon boot, it checks the device's oem/ directory for the corresponding x.cpe package and initiates installation into the /data/app/ directory as outlined below.
To maintain inter-process state across the firmware ecosystem, x.cpe exports two ContentProviders, which expose structured configuration tables storing runtime parameters, device identifiers, proxy configuration blobs, and execution flags accessible by co-installed system applications. This enables other apps in Videostrong’s ecosystem, such as their YokaTV Player streaming software, to fetch configuration parameters provided by the C2 server mentioned below.
The malware utilizes a two-stage communications protocol. It first fetches initial bootstrap configurations via an HTTP request, followed by a persistent MQTT subscription to receive commands and module download instructions.
To dynamically derive the HTTP C2 bootstrap server, it follows the following routine:
Queries content://com.release.debug.provider/configs for private_url via x.cpe.util.ExtraReadUtils .
Queries the Android system property to determine if ro.mecool.device is true.
If true, it defaults to http://mcstb.anyevonline.com:8000
If false, it dynamically generates the following: http://stb[AndroidVersion][Type].anyevonline.com:8000 .
Using the selected hostname, the client makes an HTTP POST request with an AES-encrypted JSON object containing hardware telemetry (SN, MAC, model, firmware version) to the following endpoints:
/router/config/mqtt : This endpoint provides MQTT broker details (including Broker Hostname, TCP Port, Authentication Tokens/Passwords, and the specific Topic structure: /device/{model}/{chipId}/{actio
