There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards its IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much it of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs.
In a new filing on Monday , Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30th of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30th. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs.
Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before. At a moment when the company could win over IPO investors by showing margins improving, they’re getting worse.
A chart in the filing shows this even more clearly, tracking the company’s revenue for every dollar spent on compute. Since the start of 2025, it’s been steadily growing, peaking at just over 2x this past quarter, then falling back down to 1.72x
Many indications imply that this shift in compute margins is more of a blip than a long-term problem, but it still tells us important things about the business of running a major lab. Trying to keep up with demand, Anthropic’s compute bill shot up to $10 billion for the quarter, including, as the filing notes, “$5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments, which currently costs significantly more than comparable compute procured under our multi-year commitments.” Basically, demand was growing so fast that Anthropic had to scramble for compute, which meant paying higher rates.
Some of those deals have already played out in public. Anthropic has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute, alongside multi-billion dollar deals with Nscale , Akamai and Volta . In the parlance of the industry, these are neoclouds rather than hyperscalers — smaller outfits that offer more flexible compute deals at higher rates.
Anthropic’s margins got worse in Q3 because of deals like these, and there’s no sign they’ll be able to do without them anytime soon. As the new filing puts it, “We expect compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain our largest operating expense for the foreseeable future as additional committed compute becomes available to us under multi-year arrangements with CSPs, and as we continue to invest in additional compute.”
Anthropic is still trying to lower its compute costs. In particular, the company talks quite a bit about its efforts to build its own compute base under a project it calls “Anthropic Direct.” But with demand growing so fast, those efforts aren’t going to be able to keep pace, and the neoclouds will continue to be the best option they have.
In a sense, these are champagne problems. As long as revenue is growing at nearly 50% a quarter, few investors will worry about high compute costs — and the moment demand slows down, investors may be comforted by a compute picture that has gotten a lot sunnier. But it’s a reminder of how much AI labs still depend on the trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout — and how vulnerable they are to hiccups in that process. It’s easy to imagine the data center buildout slowing down over the next year if bond markets get skittish or local opposition gets more intense. There’s not much Anthropic can do to address either of those risks, and either one would make a messy compute picture a whole lot messier.
In the meantime, the future of Anthropic and other labs will be at the mercy of compute prices.

articles.title_orig: MTA should eliminate some jobs to prepare for budget woes, watchdog writes
articles.title_zh: MTA should eliminate some jobs to prepare for budget woes, watchdog writes
articles.content_orig:
Make your contribution now and help Gothamist thrive in 2026. Donate today
Gothamist is funded by sponsors and member donations
In less than four years, the MTA could be looking at a nearly $900 million funding shortfall as spending outpaces fare revenue, according to a new analysis from the Citizens Budget Commission, which recommends cutting the workforce to close the gap.
The budget watchdog recommends sweeping job cuts to positions that it argues technology has made obsolete. The budget commission suggested the MTA allow its trains to run with just one worker, instead of two.
Train lines that have new computer-based signals, like the L and the 7, are already fully automated, as are the announcements on the trains. While the conductor opens and closes the train doors, the operator has few other duties, which include hitting a button every 20 seconds to signal they are alert. The budget commission cited the operator’s limited responsibilities as a sign the job could be cut with no impact to service.
Eliminating operator jobs on the L and 7 lines could save $36.5 million a year, according to the report . If the agency moved to phase out two people operating trains across the system, it could save $500 million a year.
The agency is in the process of installing new signals on other lines like the A, C, E, F, G, M and R lines. For now, those lines still require two people to run the trains.
The suggestion from the Citizens Budget Commission comes at a sensitive time as Transport Workers Union Local 100 negotiates a contract with the MTA for its 40,000 subway and bus workers. The MTA is expected to release its financial plan for next year in the coming weeks, which will include a 4% fare and toll increase. The board will vote on that plan in December.
“The same recommendations have been coming down for dozens of years, so there's nothing new about it,” said Transport Workers Union of America President John Samuelsen. “It's essentially a recommendation to balance alleged deficits that the MTA has off the backs of working people.”
Last year, the state legislature tried to enshrine a requirement of two MTA workers on each train into law, but Gov. Kathy Hochul vetoed the bill , leaving open the possibility that one-person train operations could happen in the future.
“Legislatively mandated staffing prevents the MTA from modernizing — as technology and best practices continue to improve — and realizing the efficiency and financial benefits,” the Citizens Budget Commission's report argues.
The Citizens Budget Commission acknowledges the MTA has become more efficient in recent years, saving a reported $576 million this year through what the agency calls “operating efficiencies.” But the report argues that without cutting labor and healthcare costs, the MTA faces a $300 million budget gap next year that will grow to $900 million by 2030. The budget commission estimates its recommended reforms could save $2.5 billion annually.
Other recommendations include streamlining fare collection on the commuter railroads by checking tickets prior to boarding, reducing the need for someone to walk through the train. The Citizens Budget Commission argues cutting more than 1,000 jobs on Metro-North and the Long Island Rail Road could save $380 million annually.
The report also recommended MTA retirees pay more in healthcare premiums, which could bring in an additional $315 million a year.
Samuelsen countered that many laborers, ironworkers, track workers, and crane operators in the MTA get paid less than their peers in the private sector, but accept that because of the generous retirement benefits.
"The CBC is right to note that we've made extraordinary progress in securing hundreds of millions of dollars in new recurring operational efficiencies," MTA spokesperson Mitch Schwartz wrote in a statement. He did not address the proposal to eliminate jobs.
Stephen Nessen covers transportation. Since 2008 he has reported on everything from Occupy Wall Street, the rebuilding of the World Trade Center site, Hurricane Sandy, to Trump’s campaign for president. His transportation reporting has taken him everywhere from the MTA’s secret Rail Control Center to the gleaming subways of Seoul. Got a tip? Email [email protected] .

articles.title_orig: Bonus PS Plus Premium Game Is Out Now for PS5
articles.title_zh: Bonus PS Plus Premium Game Is Out Now for PS5
articles.content_orig:
You have got to wait another couple of weeks to gain access to the official set of new PS Plus Premium games for this month, but in the meantime, there's been a bonus addition to the service.
Not announced or highlighted by Sony or publisher Deep Silver, the new PS5 version of Metro Redux — which improves and enhances Metro 2033 and Metro: Last Light — has been added to PS Plus Premium. The old PS4 version was on there already, but now the listing has been updated to support the PS5 edition too.
This new PS5 version brings significant improvements over the original PS4 bundle of the two intense shooters, so they are worth revisiting again if you haven't already. Here's what to expect on PS5:
The third game in the series, Metro Exodus , was added to PS Plus Extra a few months ago, so now the entire franchise is playable natively on PS5 through Sony's subscription service. Now would also be a great time to catch up, with Metro 2039 out in February 2027.
Will you use PS Plus as a way to play through the Metro games for the first time, or do you fancy revisiting any of them? Let us know in the comments below.
[source store.playstation.com ]
Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.
That’s nice. Fantastic way to enjoy these titles.
I bought both of those games on PS4 so I snagged the free PS5 upgrades instead
I've never got round to playing any of the Metro games but I've heard great things. I don't do horror, how much do they lean into that or is it more of a focus on the story and world than straight-up scares?
Cool. Nice of them to double pack.
@springer17 I can't handle scares all that much and I never felt frightened of the series, mind you I've read the novels too and they are more terrifying because it relies on the readers imagination. Think of it more like how Fallout approaches it's combat/story beats. I'd call it more psychological and existential. For me the Horror was in the reality it's my city, for others I've talked to it's the claustrophobia. But the kind of scares that jump from Western studios isn't something you have to worry about. It's built differently is what I'm trying to say, I would call the games technical achievements even before those upgrades. You should definitely give them a try if you have the time.
I was actually thinking about playing these more recently so might finally be a good time to sign up for PS+ again for a month and knock them out.
@GirlVersusGame That's certainly enough to get me to at least give them a go, they've always intrigued me but I just never got around to trying them out. Thanks for the reply.
great games - paid full price for them back in the day - might go revisit them before the new one is out in Dec

articles.title_orig: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao addresses historic crypto hack: 'There's no 100% security'
articles.title_zh: Binance founder Changpeng Zhao addresses historic crypto hack: 'There's no 100% security'
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
It has been a busy few days for Changpeng Zhao in the wake of the hack on the enormous crypto platform he co-founded, Binance.
"It's been a pretty hectic process," Zhao, better known in crypto circles as CZ , told Yahoo Finance. "But the good thing is right now the withdrawals have been restored, the systems back to normal. People are free to use the platform without any issues now. And then all user funds are covered. The users did not suffer any loss."
Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency trading platform and holds approximately $171 billion in total assets on its platform. The company is led by co-CEOs Richard Teng and Yi Le.
Hackers recently drained roughly $6.3 billion worth of digital assets from Binance on Oct. 29.
Here's what you need to know:
Blockchain intelligence firms and the FBI attributed the 20-minute raid with high confidence to TraderTraitor, an elite state-sponsored cyber unit tied to North Korea.
North Korea reportedly denied involvement.
Rather than cracking private cryptographic keys, the attackers reportedly breached internal automated transaction workflows via a Binance employee's laptop.
Read more: How to keep your crypto safe
Binance moved swiftly to stabilize the situation by guaranteeing full customer restitution, deploying corporate treasury reserves, Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) capital, and insurance funds to replenish user balances.
"There's no 100% security," CZ added. "So when you run a platform, especially a crypto platform the possibility is always there. I did not think it was going to be this big of magnitude, probably not."

articles.title_orig: Smugglers Bypass U.S. Controls to Ship HBM to China
articles.title_zh: Smugglers Bypass U.S. Controls to Ship HBM to China
articles.content_orig:
Despite U.S. export controls on advanced semiconductors to China, High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) produced by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix is reportedly being smuggled into China. Smugglers are using a method of packaging HBMs with low-end server processors to bypass export regulations, and then detaching only the memory once in China.
According to the U.S. IT media outlet The Information on Nov. 2 (local time), smugglers who have recently been siphoning Korean HBMs to China are exploiting loopholes in export regulations.
They package the HBM with a low-end server processor on a board and export it to China. They target the fact that while exporting HBM alone is subject to U.S. regulations, packaging it with a server processor classifies the package as a server processor item.
Under U.S. export regulations, the total computing power of a semiconductor package is evaluated based on the server processor, not the memory chip. The packages are disassembled upon arriving in China. Local technicians apply heat to the board to melt the solder, detach only the necessary HBM, and discard the remaining server processors.
The separation process requires highly sophisticated skills. It is reported that the failure rate is high because applying heat too quickly or for an extended period can cause the memory stack to warp or crack.
Nevertheless, the smuggling continues due to the massive profits.
A broker in his 20s who handles HBM smuggling in China told The Information that the price of a single HBM3E, which traded for several hundred dollars just a year ago, has recently soared to about $4,000. A single AI chip package requires 6 to 8 HBMs. The memory price alone amounts to $24,000 to $32,000. AI processors, servers, and power costs are separate.
The HBMs secured in this way are reportedly sold mainly to customers of Huawei, a Chinese telecommunications equipment and IT company.
According to sources familiar with Huawei’s supply chain, Huawei recently explained to some customers that its next-generation flagship AI chip, the Ascend 960DT, will largely be equipped with HBMs produced by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. Huawei introduced that the performance of the Ascend 960DT is twice as superior as existing chips, and it will be one of the powerful processors that China can produce on its own.
As it became difficult to directly purchase the necessary memory chips from Korean companies, Huawei even advised some AI chip ordering customers to secure HBMs on their own. China is clinging to securing Korean HBMs because it lacks its own production capacity.
HBM is a core component that enhances the processing performance of AI processors by quickly transmitting large amounts of data. Without securing enough HBMs, it is difficult for a high-performance AI chip to exert its full performance even if it is developed. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix account for more than 80% of the global HBM market.
The problem is that such smuggling could also act as a burden on Korean semiconductor companies. Even if Samsung Electronics and SK hynix did not directly violate export control regulations, they could become targets of U.S. government surveillance if Chinese AI chips equipped with their memory are discovered.
In fact, Taiwan’s TSMC was investigated by the U.S. government in 2024 after semiconductors it produced were found in Huawei products. Subsequently, the U.S. ordered TSMC to completely halt AI chip exports to China.
SK hynix stated, “We are strictly complying with relevant laws and regulations, including the export control regulations of the U.S. and South Korea,” adding that it has never supplied products to Huawei since the implementation of U.S. export regulations in 2020.
Meanwhile, a perception is emerging among smugglers who consider their transactions to be a patriotic act.
A broker in his 20s who smuggles memory in China told The Information regarding his work, “It is contributing to the motherland.” He reportedly does not consider himself a smuggler.
However, as smuggling competition intensifies, concerns about crackdowns are also growing.
Another smuggler who has been ordering memory semiconductors from South Korea revealed that the risk of detection is increasing as other brokers have started using the transaction routes he used.
He said, “The more people like us there are, the easier it becomes to be discovered by regulatory authorities,” adding that he plans to sell most of his company stakes next year as crackdowns by South Korea and the U.S. are expected to be further strengthened in the future.

articles.title_orig: US, Russia and China discuss trilateral meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi
articles.title_zh: US, Russia and China discuss trilateral meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi
articles.content_orig:
Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst reports on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's response to Russian attacks, warning that strikes on their infrastructure will meet a painful response.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Monday that Russia is preparing a "massive attack" on Ukraine centered on Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, accusing Moscow of seeking to exploit the historical vote to unleash strikes while the world's attention is elsewhere.
The Ukrainian leader's warning came as voters prepared to decide which party controls Congress, a result that could also influence Washington's future response to Russian President Vladimir Putin's almost five-year war in Ukraine.
In a post on X, Zelenskyy went on to urge the Trump administration to increase pressure on Moscow, warning that Russia could exploit the elections to target Ukraine's battered energy infrastructure and supply routes.
DRONE STRIKE SINKS SHIP IN NATO WATERS AS ZELENSKYY WARNS OF LOOMING ‘MASSIVE STRIKE’
Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. (Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik/Kremlin Pool Photo/Efrem Lukatsky/AP)
"We have intel that Russia is preparing a new massive attack on our country – primarily targeting energy and logistics," Zelenskyy said in his nightly address.
"The assumption is basically that tomorrow the world will be watching the American midterms, and what is happening here in Ukraine, along with our difficulties with air defense and Patriot missiles, will be overlooked."
Zelenskyy's warning came hours after Russian forces struck a school being used to distribute humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, a settlement in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region.
At least 26 people, including police officers and first responders, were killed, five others were injured and others remained missing, according to the Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda .
ZELENSKYY PRESSURES US AND EUROPE FOR MORE 'AIR DEFENSE' ASSISTANCE AMID ONGOING WAR WITH RUSSIA
Ukraine's largest private energy company reports 90% of generation capacity damaged by Russian attacks, leaving over 1 million without power during freezing temperatures. (Reuters)
In his X post, Zelenskyy urged the U.S. and its allies to warn Putin that continued attacks on Ukraine would bring serious economic consequences.
"We need signals from the world to Russia that will make them feel that terror is no good, that it will bring no gains, and that as long as this war continues, their oil will burn, and they will not be able to make money doing business with the world," Zelenskyy warned.
"We must not play games with Russia's oil or gas revenues," he added.
"We must put pressure on Russia in such a way that it has no alternative but to end this war. America can do this."
TRUMP ANNOUNCES IMMEDIATE ENERGY CEASEFIRE BETWEEN RUSSIA AND UKRAINE
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, left talks with President Donald Trump and members of his Cabinet during a lunch meeting at the White House on Oct. 17, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)
President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has sought to negotiate an end to the war with the help of special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner , both of whom have been involved in diplomatic efforts with Moscow.
Zelenskyy told Fox News in a Sunday interview that Ukraine would suspend strikes on Russian oil refineries for a month if Washington provided Patriot missile interceptors during the same period, potentially opening the door to diplomacy.
The State Department approved the potential sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 interceptor missiles to Ukraine for an estimated $2.1 billion, according to Reuters.
The proposed sale could provide a significant boost to Ukraine's air defenses if finalized, although the delivery timeline is uncertain.
TRUMP SAYS US WILL LET UKRAINE MAKE PATRIOT MISSILES IN MAJOR POLICY SHIFT
First Lady Melania Trump, left, and civilians being evacuated from Oleshky, Ukraine, in October 2022 during the early days of the Russia-Ukraine war. (Umit Bektas/Reuters; Alexander Ermochenko/Reuters)
On Monday, Ukraine also accused Moscow of exploiting a U.S.-backed humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky , in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, to strengthen Russian military positions.
Nearly 800 people were evacuated during the six-day humanitarian pause, according to first lady Melania Trump, with the White House clarifying that she helped broker the arrangement.
Ukraine's General Staff accused Russian forces of using the humanitarian pause to rotate troops, reinforce their defenses and improve battlefield logistics.
"Under the ceasefire introduced for the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, units of the Defence Forces of Ukraine ensured that the ceasefire was observed and acted exclusively within the framework of the agreements reached," the General Staff said in a statement on X.

articles.title_orig: Single check-in for those in Hong Kong transit under scheme with mainland China
articles.title_zh: Single check-in for those in Hong Kong transit under scheme with mainland China
articles.content_orig:
Those travelling from Hangzhou or Wuhan can have bags checked through to final destination overseas under new one-stop service launched on Tuesday
Travellers flying from Hangzhou or Wuhan to overseas destinations via Hong Kong on different airlines can have their baggage checked through to the final destination under a newly launched service that aims to step up the connections between mainland Chinese cities and other countries.
Under the new one-stop service that launched on Tuesday, travellers departing from Hangzhou Xiaoshan International Airport or Wuhan Tianhe International Airport will not need to check in their baggage again when transferring through Hong Kong, even if they are flying on a different airline on the next leg of their journey.
“Hong Kong International Airport is launching a game-changing service,” Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said.
